items.statement_scope: Whole separately stated original Problem3.6(D), attributed to B.Clark: is there a homology3-sphere (or any3-manifold) obtained by n-surgery on infinitely many distinct knots? The chosen paper explicitly quotes this exact D problem and constructs a family for every fixed integer n; choosing |n|=1 gives the required homology sphere. Both original homology-sphere and general3-manifold alternatives are retained. Parts3.6(A)-(C), the stronger4-manifold extension and the two construction families are not counted as extra questions.

standard_prerequisites: Standard integer Dehn-surgery homology calculation: surgery coefficient |n|=1 on a knot in S3 gives an integral homology3-sphere; source explicitly uses this onphysical1.
Kirby calculus, annulus twisting, inherited orientations and preferred-longitude framing as defined in the paper.

For the first family: the cited bridge-number growth theorem, hyperbolic Dehn-surgery theorem and Neumann-Zagier volume asymptotics; author-attributed HIKMOT certified computations are preserved at Claim2.5.

For the second family: the standard surgery description of infinite cyclic covers and Alexander polynomial from Rolfsen Chapter7, cited at Lemma3.17; the elementary carving extension criterion is fully stated in Lemma3.9.
source_caveats: Original problem is credited exactly as B.Clark, distinct from collection editor RobKirby and the four proof authors.
The paper Claim2.5physical6 expressly says SnapPy hyperbolicity calculations were certified by HIKMOT. This is the authors recorded certification claim; no new verification run is asserted.

Remark2.6physical7 expressly says the listed numerical volumes of three optional output manifolds are not HIKMOT-verified. Those approximate volumes are not used as a substitute for the existence or distinctness proof.

The second-family n=0 branch cites the earlier Abe-Jong-Omae-Takeuchi2013 result. The original homology-sphere task is covered locally by the n=1 family with Alexander-degree distinctness, and the first family also covers general integer slopes. No extra counted theorem is extracted.

(D) (B. Clark) Is there a homology 3-sphere (or any 3-manifold) which can be obtained by
    n-surgery on an infinite number of distinct knots?
      Remarks: Lickorish gave an example obtained from two knots [652,1977,Proc. Amer.
      Math. Soc.]. Problems 1.15 and 1.16 ask whether this is possible for S 3 (Property P)
      or S 1 × S 2 (Property R). It seems likely that the Poincaré homology sphere can be ob-
      tained only from +1-surgery on the right-handed trefoil knot (or, reversing orientation,
      from -1-surgery on the left-handed trefoil knot).
